# SHORT FORM. Why people want what others have. Brian's script, word for word (do not edit the words).
# Payoff: we compare ourselves to whoever's next to us, and once we get the thing we picture the next one.
# Running gag: "But what he doesn't know…" chain. Narrator bet: "I thought it ended with Doug." Flip: the man in the wheelchair.
# Victor, the drivers, Doug and the man in the wheelchair are fictional (Brian's story). The psychology is real (sources.md).
[#q] Why the heck do people want what *others have?
[#problem] See, Victor had a problem. He worked really hard to buy his dream car, a {*Lamborghini.|Lamborghini.}
[#light] And now he’s sitting in it, stuck at a {!red light.|red light.}
[#heli] Then a helicopter flies right over him. [#looks] Victor looks up and thinks, “Man, I wish I had *that.”
[#nolights] No red lights up there.
[#gwagon] But what he doesn’t know is that the guy next to him in a G-Wagon is thinking, “Man, I wish I had that Lamborghini.”
[#regular] But what he doesn’t know is that the guy in the regular car is thinking, “Man, I wish I had that G-Wagon.”
[#doug] But what he doesn’t know is that Doug, walking by, is thinking, “Man, I’d take *any of those cars.”
[#bet] Honestly? I thought it ended with Doug.
[#picture] See, Victor used to picture himself behind the wheel of that Lamborghini. [#now] Now he’s finally in it, picturing himself in the {*helicopter.|helicopter.}
[#green] The light turns green. The cars pull away.
[#wheel] But what Doug doesn’t know is that a man in a wheelchair is watching him walk by, [#walk] thinking, “I wish I could {*walk|walk} again.”
[#moral] Sometimes we get so caught up looking at what other people have that we forget to {*appreciate|appreciate} what we already have.
[#end] What’s one thing you have today that you used to {*wish|wish} for?
[#cta] Still here? Then that means you enjoyed the video. So *follow and *like for more.
